raw_response:
I will still plant the way I usually do: start from last year, then adjust a little, not turn everything upside down. On 13.5 mu with just two people, I have to keep labor and cash in mind. Cotton is still my main crop, because I know it best and it brings cash, so I will leave more land to cotton and keep maize and wheat on smaller pieces. I have well water, so I will not be stingy with the key irrigations. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing yield costs me more, so I will feed the crop a bit on the safe side, especially nitrogen. I will use improved seed where I have seen it work nearby, and for maize I will use hybrid seed because that is already common and the yield is steadier. Wheat and maize here can yield well if water and fertilizer do not fall short, but I will not count on the very highest demonstration-field numbers. I will set my plan at a level I feel I can actually manage on my own land.
